summary: Ram Chandra Dhungana worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Assistant Editor for Ancient Nepal (attested 1973) and for the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1974).

Ram Chandra Kak was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Sri Pratap College and under John Marshall (1914–1919). He served as Superintendent of the Jammu and Kashmir Research and Archaeological Department (~1914) and Director of Archæology and Research (1919–1929).

Ram Chandra Pandeya was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale and T. R. V. Murti. At the University of Delhi, he was Professor and Head of Buddhist Studies (attested 1971) and acharya (attested 1996).

Ram Karan Sharma was an Indologist and linguist who earned his MA at Patna University and PhD at UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He was Vice Chancellor of Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (1974–1980) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1984–1985).

Ram Mohan Roy was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He founded the Atmiya Sabha (1814), Presidency University (1816), Anglo-Hindu School (1822), Mirat-ul-Akhbar (1822), Vedanta College (1826), the Brahmo Samaj (1828), and the Calcutta Unitarian Committee.

Ram Niwas Pandey works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology, completing doctoral studies under Hit Narayan Jha.

Ram Prasad Bhatt is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who completed doctoral studies at Hemwati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University (2003–2006). He held posts at the University of Leipzig (2002–2003) and the University of Hamburg (2003).

Ram Shankar Bhattacharya was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Raghunatha Shastri. He held posts as an instructor at Tikmani Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya and as a research assistant at Banaras Hindu University and the All-India Kashiraj Trust.

Ram Shankar Tripathi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He headed the Buddhist Philosophy department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1977, 1989–1998) and served as Dean of Śabdavidyā at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2001).

Historian Ram Sharan Sharma studied at Patna University and earned his PhD at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and Wilhelm Rau. He was professor and head of history at Patna University (1958–1973) and professor and dean at Delhi University (1973–1978).
Rama Kant Agnihotri is a linguist and Indologist who completed his DPhil studies at York University (1973–1975). He served on an editorial board at the University of Delhi from 1980 to 2010.
Rama Mishra Shastri was an Indologist and philosopher who held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, including Professor (attested 1882–1889) and Assistant Professor of Sāṅkhya (attested 1914).

Rama Nath Sharma is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Raghunatha Sharma and Ram Prasad Tripathi, earning a PhD from the University of Rochester. He taught at Rochester (1971–1976) before becoming a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1976).

Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar studied under Martin Haug, earning degrees from Mumbai and Göttingen. He served as professor at Elphinstone College (~1868–1882) and Deccan College (~1882–1893), and later as Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (~1893–1894).

Indologist Ramanath Pandey earned his PhD from Ranchi University and a BA from Delhi University. He worked as a Research Officer at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (2004–2022) and Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 2008), and became Professor at Parshwanath Vidyapeeth (2025).

Ramanatha Dikshita was an Indologist who worked in the Sadholal Research Department at Sarasvati Bhavana (attested 1944) and served as Head of the Veda Department at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi (attested 1970).

Ramaprasad Chanda was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Dhaka College and Scottish Church College. He worked at the Archaeological Survey of India (1917–1919) and was Superintendent of the Archaeological Section at the Indian Museum, Kolkata (1921–1932).
Ram Prasad Tripathi was an Indologist and linguist who held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, where he served as a former vice-chancellor (attested 1976) and was affiliated in 2001.

Indologist Ramaranjan Mukherji earned degrees at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University. He served as Vice Chancellor of the University of Burdwan (1970–1984) and Rabindra Bharati University (~1979–1987), and later Chancellor of the National Sanskrit University.

Ramashastri Bhagavatacharya was an Indology scholar who served as an Assistant Professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and as an instructor at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi (both attested 1891).
